meta.title: The Kids Who Hacked the World, Part 2: The Teens Who Stole the Next Xbox
meta.working_title: The Teens Who Stole the Xbox Before It Existed (The Kids Who Hacked the World, Part 2)
meta.device: A big wall of company logos (as plain name tiles) that turn green one by one as the gang gets inside, plus a gamer-tag roster card for each member that flips to a mugshot silhouette when they're arrested.
meta.style: Internet-crime caper in the house 2D style, Gumball/t-shirt character style (same as Part 1). Painted plates: a Canada-US border crossing, a teen's bedroom full of consoles and wires, a recycling yard of old dev-kit consoles, a game-studio office at night, a convention hall, Microsoft's campus at night, a courtroom. Neon green on black for the console world, cool greys for the law. Real people stylised, no likeness; names from public court records. No hacking how-to: methods described only as 'leaked passwords' at high level. A member's later suicide handled with care: no method or self-harm detail, a helpline card on screen. SFX under the VO (console boot chimes, keyboard clicks, door rams, gavel), music at combine.
meta.source: English compilation transcript 'The Kids Who Hacked the World', segment 1 (~4,900 words), based on Wired's reporting and Darknet Diaries; public court facts only. Sponsor read cut, self-harm details removed. Fully rewritten.

shots.vo: March 2014. A young Canadian and his dad drive to the US border. He's going to pick up a car bumper from an online friend.
shots.visual: A family car pulling up to a border booth; a long queue of cars.

shots.vo: The officer scans his passport. A strange word pops up on the screen. 'Xenomega?' That's his online gaming name.
shots.visual: A border officer's screen showing a gamer tag; the officer raising an eyebrow.

shots.vo: Officers surround the car. He's arrested. The FBI has been after him for years. He's part of a gang that broke into Microsoft, Epic Games, and even a US Army simulator project.
shots.visual: Officers at the car; the logo wall behind lights up green.
Title over the logo wall.
shots.onscreen: THE KIDS WHO HACKED THE WORLD · PART 2
shots.anim: Console boot chime; title glows green.

shots.vo: 2001. Microsoft launches its first Xbox. A huge black box with a giant controller. A boy in Canada called David Pokora falls in love with Halo.
shots.visual: A kid in front of a chunky black console, controller in hand.

shots.vo: But David cares more about how the machine works. He joins online forums where fans tweak their consoles, and he writes mods that change Halo's physics and weather.
shots.visual: A forum page on screen; a game world where the rain switches to snow.

shots.vo: The Xbox 360 is harder to tinker with. You need a developer kit, a special console only approved studios get. Then a batch of old ones turns up at a recycling yard, and they get resold online.
shots.visual: A scrapyard; a pile of consoles with 'DEV KIT' stickers; one picked out.
shots.anim: A hand lifts a kit from the pile.

shots.vo: With a dev kit, David can see Microsoft's private network for game developers, where unreleased games are tested. He posts screenshots and becomes a star of the scene. His grades slide.
shots.visual: Screenshots of 'unreleased' games pinned on a forum; a report card with Ds.

shots.vo: He sells Call of Duty cheats online for 100 dollars a half hour, and says he made up to 8,000 dollars a day. The game's publisher sends legal letters. He ignores them.
shots.visual: A shop screen 'CHEATS $100/30MIN'; legal letters piling up unopened.

shots.vo: The scene brings a crew together. In Perth, Australia, a 14-year-old called Dylan Wheeler, already suspended for hacking his school, twice.
shots.visual: A roster card flips in: 'SUPERDAE · 14 · PERTH'.
shots.anim: Card flips in with a ping.

shots.vo: In New Jersey, Sanadodeh Nesheiwat, 24, who takes consoles apart with a soldering iron. Online: Sonic.
shots.visual: A desk with a soldering iron, oscilloscope and console parts.

shots.vo: And in Delaware, Justin May, a few years older than David, who buys a dev kit from him. Online: MTW.
shots.visual: A roster card: 'MTW · DELAWARE'.

shots.vo: Later they're joined by two more: Austin Alcala, 16, from Indiana, and Nathan Leroux, 18, from Maryland, who dreams of making games.
shots.visual: Two more roster cards slide in beside the others.

shots.vo: 2011. Dylan gets a leaked list of usernames and passwords from a gaming forum. Some people reuse the same password everywhere. That's how he gets into Epic Games, the studio behind Gears of War.
shots.visual: A leaked list scrolls; one line glows; a door marked EPIC swings open.

shots.vo: David tells himself he has rules: no customer data, no credit cards. Just the games. Then they find an early version of Gears of War 3.
shots.visual: A folder on a server labelled 'GEARS 3 - EARLY BUILD'.

shots.vo: Sonic downloads hundreds of gigabytes overnight, burns it to eight Blu-ray discs, and posts them to David in a package marked 'wedding videos'.
shots.visual: A stack of discs; a parcel with 'WEDDING VIDEOS' scrawled on it.

shots.vo: Days after it's shared around, the game leaks to the public. It's news everywhere. Epic calls in the FBI.
shots.visual: A news ticker 'GEARS 3 LEAKED'; an FBI badge slides in.

shots.vo: The others panic and go quiet. Dylan doesn't. He keeps logging in, finds a list of the company's master passwords, and even watches staff through their office webcams.
shots.visual: A boy in a dark room watching a grid of office webcam feeds.

shots.vo: The others can't resist. One by one: Microsoft, EA, Valve, Activision, Blizzard. Then companies far beyond games.
shots.visual: The logo wall of name tiles flipping green fast.
shots.anim: Tiles flip green one by one.

shots.vo: Intel, AMD, Disney, Warner Bros, Google. Around 25 major companies in total.
shots.visual: A counter climbing to 25.

shots.vo: In 2012 two members find a link from a game studio to a US Army system, and an Apache helicopter simulator being built for the military. They hesitate. Then they download it.
shots.visual: A helicopter outline on a military screen; a nervous cursor hovering over 'download'.

shots.vo: They joke about what they'd call their gang in prison. 'Xbox Underground' sounds cool. They laugh. Not for long.
shots.visual: The crew's roster cards with a jokey prison-gang name tag.

shots.vo: August 2012. Inside Microsoft, they find a locked-down folder: designs for the next Xbox, codename Durango. It will become the Xbox One.
shots.visual: A blueprint of a console with 'DURANGO' stamped on it.

shots.vo: The parts are available to buy. So they order them, and Nathan builds a working copy at home. Then they try to sell it to a buyer in the Seychelles for 5,000 dollars.
shots.visual: A kitchen table with parts; a finished console glowing.

shots.vo: Justin offers to post it. It never arrives. Then Dylan, without asking the others, puts photos of the prototype up on eBay.
shots.visual: An eBay-style auction page; bids climbing.

shots.vo: The auction goes viral. Microsoft gets it taken down, and Dylan starts giving interviews. The rest of the gang are furious.
shots.visual: A video-interview tile with Dylan; angry chat bubbles from the others.

shots.vo: Then an 18-year-old fan offers them a real prototype. He has been sneaking into Microsoft's campus for months, using copied access cards.
shots.visual: Microsoft-style campus at night; a teen in a hoodie with a backpack.

shots.vo: One night he walks into an office, puts three prototype consoles in his backpack, and walks out.
shots.visual: An open-plan office at night; a backpack being zipped over console boxes.

shots.vo: A week later Microsoft offers him a job he'd applied for. Weeks after that, security cameras catch up with him, and he loses it.
shots.visual: A 'YOU'RE HIRED' email, then a CCTV still with a red circle.

shots.vo: The arrests come one by one. Nathan's house is raided. Then Sonic's. In February 2013, Australian police arrest Dylan. In 2014, Austin, and then David at the border.
shots.visual: The roster cards flip to grey silhouettes, one by one.

shots.vo: The FBI's case is huge: chat logs, call recordings, years of evidence. Much of it, according to the charges, came from someone called 'Person A', from Wilmington, Delaware.
shots.visual: An indictment page with 'PERSON A' circled.

shots.vo: The gang only knew one person from Wilmington. Many came to believe it was Justin, who had been arrested at a games convention years before. It was never officially confirmed.
shots.visual: The MTW card with a question mark over it.

shots.vo: In the US, the four plead guilty. David and Sonic each get 18 months in prison. Austin, who helps the FBI on another case, gets probation.
shots.visual: A gavel; sentence cards: 18 MONTHS, 18 MONTHS, PROBATION.

shots.vo: David later works in cyber security. Sonic struggles under strict probation, and is jailed again before finally getting back on his feet.
shots.visual: David at a security-company desk; Sonic at a window, then smiling.

shots.vo: Nathan, the youngest and least involved, served two years. After release, Holly, as she was later known, took her own life. If you're struggling, please reach out to someone.
shots.visual: A single lit window at night; a helpline card fades in.
shots.onscreen: NEED HELP? CALL OR TEXT 988 (US) · FIND A HELPLINE: findahelpline.com

shots.vo: In Australia, Dylan pleaded not guilty, then left for the Czech Republic before his case ended. In 2017 Justin was arrested for separate frauds, and later sentenced to years in prison.
shots.visual: A plane leaving Perth; then a separate cell door.

shots.vo: Next: two British teenagers who broke into the email of the head of the CIA.
shots.visual: A CIA-style seal with an inbox icon; NEXT card.
End card.
shots.onscreen: THE KIDS WHO HACKED THE WORLD · PART 3 NEXT

hooks: A group of teenagers had the next Xbox before Microsoft announced it. One of them built it at his kitchen table.
He got arrested at the border because of his gamer tag.

fixes: Pokora arrested March 2014 at the Lewiston-Queenston crossing; first foreign hacker convicted in the US for stealing trade secrets (Pokora and Nesheiwat 18 months, 2015).
Gamer tags: Pokora 'Xenomega', Wheeler 'SuperDaE', Nesheiwat 'Sonic', May 'MTW' per Wired.
Gears of War 3 early build leaked 2011 (source mixed '3' and 'II'; kept '3').
Apache simulator: Army's AH-64D simulator being developed by Zombie Studios (per DOJ).
Person A link to Justin May is the members' belief, stated as unconfirmed.
Justin May arrested 2017 for separate Cisco/Microsoft return fraud; sentence stated generally ('years in prison').
Dylan Wheeler's mother's conviction cut (disputed by Wheeler).
Nathan/Holly LeRoux's death: no method or self-harm detail; helpline card shown.
Method kept to 'reused leaked passwords' only; no specific passwords or tooling.
cuts: Specific passwords and access details cut.
